faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.intro: Answers to the most common questions about our trainings.

items.question: What is agentic engineering?
items.answer: Agentic engineering means using AI agents to generate and verify code, in collaboration with an engineer. The engineer directs the agents, guards quality and decides where human judgement is needed.

items.question: Who are the trainings for?
items.answer: The Basic training targets complete DevOps teams: developers, QA / testers, ops and engineering managers training alongside their team. The Advanced training is for tech leads, staff+ engineers and managers rolling out agentic workflows team-wide. The training pages give more detail per training.

items.question: What prior knowledge do I need?
items.answer: For the Basic training we expect you to be comfortable with git and the command line and to write features in at least one language (TypeScript, Python, Go, etc.). Experience with agentic engineering is not required. Bring your own laptop with Claude Code or OpenCode installed and at least a Claude Pro subscription. The Advanced training requires the Basic training or comparable hands-on experience with Claude Code.

items.question: What will I be able to do afterwards?
items.answer: After the Basic training you ship a working feature on a starter repo — with tests, hooks and green CI — recognise failure modes of AI-generated code, work test-first with an agent, set up quality gates and use MCP servers in real workflows. After the Advanced training you leave with a peer-reviewed 90-day rollout plan, orchestrate subagents at team scale and have observability and cost guardrails in place.

items.question: What is the format and duration?
items.answer: The Basic training takes two days (16 hours), the Advanced training one day (8 hours). Both are available as open enrollment, in-company or remote.

items.question: Do you work with Claude Code? Which tools are covered?
items.answer: Yes, Claude Code is central; OpenCode works too. You also work with MCP servers, skills, hooks, subagents and CI integration.

items.question: What does it cost, and are there discounts?
items.answer: Both trainings cost €999 per person, excluding VAT. However, the announced Basic Training now has a discount of 30% until the 1st of August

items.question: Can you deliver in-company?
items.answer: Yes, we deliver both trainings in-company as well, on site or remote. Get in touch via the contact form to discuss the options.

items.question: In which language is the training taught?
items.answer: We teach the trainings in Dutch and in English.

why.title: Why learn agentic engineering
why.tagline: AI scales the breadth. You set the depth.
paragraphs: The work is shifting. The scarce skill is no longer typing code as fast as possible, but directing agents and verifying their work. Whoever masters that suddenly does far more on their own. Think of the boilerplate that has to be written, or the tests you otherwise keep putting off. The time you win back goes to the questions that demand human insight.

To do that, it helps to follow training so you too can judge where an agent fits best, and which tools you are better off giving it or not. The trouble with agents is that they often sound certain in their answers, whether right or wrong. Being aware of that and steering for it is what separates using an agent from deploying one. Give an agent free rein over your system (read: accept all) and the consequences can hit hard. The difference between an agent that moves you forward and one that does damage is not luck but craftsmanship: it shows in scoping the agent well and always verifying. That craftsmanship is what you learn in these trainings.

Along the way you learn a structured way of working, and a handhold in the sprawl of new AI concepts. You do not need to memorize every term; you learn an approach that holds up while the tools change fast.
why.qe: For quality engineers this is a logical step. Verification is your craft. In a world full of agents, you become the layer that makes their work reliably deployable. Your role does not disappear; it only grows more important.
